qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Exclusive state-granted franchise territory for electric and gas distribution in CT, MA, and NH creates an insurmountable geographic barrier and captive customer base. Tariffs are set via cost-of-service rate-base regulation with formulaic cost recovery. However, allowed returns are capped by state utility commissions and FERC, exposing the firm to regulatory lag and disallowances.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). Traditional regulated utility anchor falls in Mauboussin Tier 4 baseline persistence (5-10 years). Faces severe unhedged terminal macrotrend headwinds: Energy Transition capital misallocation (over $2.5B cumulative impairments and exit costs on offshore wind joint ventures) and Structural Cost of Capital/Inflation headwinds where massive ongoing capex ($4B+/year) and heavy debt load ($30B+) collide with hostile regulatory rate-setting in Connecticut (PURA).
qualitative.evidence: Eversource operates regulated electric, natural gas, and water utilities across Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire serving ~4.4M customers. While possessing an exclusive territorial distribution monopoly, its 10-year median ROIC is just ~4.9%, structurally limited by utility rate-base regulation and heavy debt. Annual capex ($4.48B in 2024, $4.16B in 2025) perpetually exceeds operating cash flow, resulting in negative free cash flow (-$45M in 2025) and continuous debt dilution (total debt reached $30.28B by year-end 2025 against recurring earnings of ~$1.7B). Its foray into offshore wind ended in a disastrous divestiture to GIP with $1.95B in 2023 impairments, $524M in 2024 closing losses, and continued contingent liability drag in 2025-2026. Coupled with an adversarial regulatory climate at Connecticut PURA, Eversource lacks secular compounding resilience and fails the 15-year CAP threshold.
